Not to be confused with [List of storms named Gilma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_storms_named_Gilma "List of storms named Gilma"), [List of storms named Hilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_storms_named_Hilda "List of storms named Hilda"), [List of storms named Tilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_storms_named_Tilda "List of storms named Tilda"), or [List of storms named Wilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_storms_named_Wilda "List of storms named Wilda").

The name **Gilda** has been used for 13 [tropical cyclones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone "Tropical cyclone") worldwide. Three of them occurred in the [Atlantic Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean"), nine in the West [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean"), and one in the South-West [Indian Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean").

In the Atlantic:

*   [Tropical Storm Gilda (1954)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Gilda_(1954) "Tropical Storm Gilda (1954)") – caused 29 fatalities in Honduras before making landfall in Belize and Mexico
*   [Tropical Storm Gilda (1973)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Gilda_(1973) "Tropical Storm Gilda (1973)") – the first documented tropical cyclone on record to transition into a [subtropical cyclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtropical_cyclone "Subtropical cyclone")

In the West Pacific:

*   [Tropical Storm Gilda (1952)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Gilda_(1952) "Tropical Storm Gilda (1952)") (T5205)

According to the NOAA HURDAT2 best‑track database (the file

*Hurricanes that originated off the west coast are those whose first
reported position falls within a 60 nautical‑mile buffer of the Baja
California‑Sur and Baja California peninsulas; the east‑coast count is
defined analogously for the Gulf/Caribbean shoreline of *Mexico*.*

The **2010–2019** decade therefore shows the largest absolute
difference ( **8 hurricanes**).
